title: Why Is Christmas Suddenly Under Attack in India?
description:
#Himdutva #mobviolence #christmas

What happens when faith turns into fear?
When belief stops being personal — and starts policing others?

In this video, we look at the disturbing rise of religious vigilantism in India, where Christmas decorations are torn down, vendors are harassed, and public spaces become battlegrounds for identity politics.

This isn’t about attacking religion.
It’s about defending the idea that belief should never be enforced through fear.

From vandalised malls to moral policing, from constitutional rights to street-level intimidation — this video examines how faith, power, and insecurity collide, and why a society that once celebrated diversity now struggles with its own reflection.

If you believe freedom of belief should apply to everyone — not just those in power — this video is for you.

00:00 – 00:55 | Intro
A Christmas tree destroyed. A mall in chaos. A question nobody wants to answer.

00:55 – 01:55 | When Decorations Become a Threat
Why something as harmless as a Santa hat suddenly becomes “anti-national.”

01:55 – 03:05 | The Myth of Hurt Sentiments
How offense becomes a weapon — and who really benefits.

03:05 – 04:20 | Constitution vs Crowd
What the law actually says about religion, and how mobs replace it.

04:20 – 05:30 | Belief vs Bullying
The fine line between faith and force.

05:30 – 06:40 | Hypocrisy Without Borders
Why celebrating your culture abroad but rejecting others at home makes no sense.

06:40 – 07:45 | When Faith Becomes an Identity Weapon
From diversity to dominance — how religions lose their soul.

07:45 – 08:50 | The Cost of Turning Belief Into Power
What we lose when faith becomes a political tool.

08:50 – 09:49 | The Final Question
Is this devotion — or just fear dressed up as faith?

comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE OF ATTACKS ON CHRISTIANS DURING CHRISTMAS

Attacks on Christians during Christmas are not random incidents or isolated acts of hatred.
They are the direct outcome of structural and legal failures that weaken constitutional protections.

1️⃣ UNCONSTITUTIONAL ANTI-CONVERSION LAWS

Most attacks on Christians occur in states that have “anti-conversion” laws.

• These laws presume conversion is fraudulent
• They criminalise prayer, worship, and personal faith choices
• They empower vigilantes to harass and attack believers

Article 25 of the Constitution guarantees every Indian the freedom of conscience and the right to profess, practice, and propagate religion.
Any law that restricts peaceful conversion violates this fundamental right.

2️⃣ STATE-SANCTIONED DISCRIMINATION AGAINST DALIT CHRISTIANS

Another major root cause is the removal of Scheduled Caste status when Dalits convert to Christianity.

• Caste discrimination is determined by birth, not religion
• Conversion does not erase social stigma or exclusion
• Denying SC status after conversion is institutional discrimination

This policy forces Dalits to choose between constitutional rights and freedom of faith, which is unjust and unequal.

3️⃣ LEGITIMISATION OF MOB VIOLENCE

When the law: • Treats conversion as a crime
• Withdraws legal protection from converts
• Signals hostility toward minority faiths

It creates an environment where mobs feel morally and legally justified in attacking churches, homes, and prayer gatherings — even on Christmas.

4️⃣ WHY CONDEMNATION ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH

Condemning violence after it happens is necessary, but insufficient.

Unless we: • Repeal or reform anti-conversion laws
• Restore SC rights regardless of religion
• Enforce law equally against vigilantes

Attacks will continue to repeat every Christmas.

CONCLUSION

The root cause of attacks on Christians is not celebration or prayer.
It is unconstitutional laws and systemic discrimination.

Defending Christians’ right to celebrate Christmas is not about religion alone.
It is about protecting the Indian Constitution and rule of law.
